en: The Dharma Master Tripitaka Prajñā transmits: At one time, the World-Honored One Śākyamuni Tathāgata, having eradicated suffering and affliction, manifested great supernormal powers and flew through the air with his great alms bowl.
He resided upon the summit of the Snow Mountains together with five hundred bhikṣus, ten thousand bodhisattvas, and the eight classes of devas and nāgas.
A great multitude of immeasurable size had gathered together to hear the Dharma. At that time, the assembly was weary and food was difficult to obtain.
Then the World-Honored One entered the Great Compassion Samādhi (*mahāmaitrī-samādhi*). From within the radiance, a great alms bowl of the Tathāgata surged forth and departed through the air;
no one knew where it went. The great assembly was struck with alarm and doubt. Thereupon, the Buddha’s great bowl returned, filled to the brim with rice.
At that time, the Tathāgata arose from his meditative concentration and addressed the great assembly, saying, "All of you should eat this.
Having spoken these words, the great assembly rejoiced and ate the rice from the bowl; yet it remained inexhaustible.
Its fragrance filled the trichiliocosm, and those in the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals were all fully satiated.

Thereupon, Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying: "By what supernatural power does the Tathāgata cause this great bowl to fly, so as to satisfy the great assembly and relieve the suffering of sentient beings in the three miserable realms and the eight difficult conditions?

How may we and those in future ages who seek the Dharma and cultivate the Way practice this Dharma to accomplish the work of a Buddha and benefit sentient beings? We pray only that the Great [Teacher]..."
The Holy One spoke this essential Dharma. The Buddha addressed Mañjuśrī: "It is thus, it is so, noble son.
I shall now expound that Dharma for the benefit of sentient beings and the great advantage of practitioners.

In the past, when I was a great ṛṣi dwelling in a cave on the Snowy Mountains, I had long since ceased taking food or clothing, having no means to obtain them. At that time, I had ten thousand disciples."
We dwelt together in ascetic practices. A king of the garuḍas came and said to me, "I pray that you, Great Seer, will take up your alms-bowl and travel to the heavens and the human realm;
having filled it with food and clothing, return to provide offerings to the great assembly.
At that time, I, the seer, granted his request. Then the garuḍa king took up the bowl and flew through the trichiliocosm, covering it all in a single moment.
The bowl filled with food and robes was brought back; the great assembly rejoiced and all attained peace and security.
You should know that the seer of that time was none other than my own self. I shall now explain his method:

first, select a pure place—a deep mountain, a secluded forest, or among high crags where no people dwell—by the side of a great river, a vast ocean, or a clear spring. There, one should sever food intake, practice ascetic discipline, and consume the five leaves.
Using pine needles and various fruits and foods, one should recite the Tathāgata’s Great Alms-bowl mantra and form its mudrā.
Without ceasing the sound for six periods of the day and night, one will achieve accomplishment within three days; this is the characteristic of the seal.

First, place the right hand at the heart with the palm facing upward. Next, cover it with the left hand, placing the right palm over the left so that the tips of the right ring fingers touch the tips of the left thumbs, and the tips of the left thumbs touch the tips of the right ring fingers.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ lokapāla-deśita dhara dhara mahā-brahma-buddha-dhāraṇī svāhā.* One should recite this mantra one million times.
This is the Dharma-seal mantra; its great power shall be for the sake of all.
The Tathāgata’s spiritual power shall protect them. One should form this mudrā and recite this mantra; then one will immediately attain accomplishment.
If there are sentient beings in the hells or among the hungry ghosts, by reciting it one hundred and eight times, those in the hells and hungry ghosts will be satiated with all kinds of food.
If one travels through wildernesses and likewise forms this mudrā and recites this mantra, the spirits and demons of the wilderness will not [harm] them.
It is playful. Therefore, his bowl flies through the ten directions at will. When upholding this dharma, one should summon the Kāpota-garuḍa King as a messenger;
by the supernatural power of the Tathāgata, that king is able to serve him accordingly.
The practitioner, knowing this, shall find the empty bowl turn of its own accord when he dispatches the mantra.

The Mantra for Turning the Alms Bowl:
Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Namo saṃghāya | Namo tārāpate | Cāra-dhāraṇī parivartadhāraṇī parivarta svāhā.
When performing the ritual, one should purify a single room and sprinkle the floor with scented water.

Prostrate to the Buddhas of the four directions and summon a young boy, instructing him to wash his hands and face and also to prostrate to the Buddha. Upon that ground, spread a clean woolen rug and take a single alms bowl.
Wash [the object] clean with scented water and place it upon a felt mat. Take a pure cloth and place it inside a bowl.
Summon a youth and have him kneel with both knees pressed against the bowl, grasping the ground with both hands. The mantra-practitioner recites the mantra repeatedly, saying:
"Yun-zhuan-he-he ji-zhuan" (The wheel turns, he-he, it turns). Furthermore, invoke the Three Jewels and all the divine kings with mantras.
Namo buddhāya. Namo dharmāya. Namo saṃghāya. Tadyathā: īme īme mine mine svāhā.
Whenever one wishes to recite this mantra, first recite it twenty-one times to perform the invocation; thereafter, recite the mantra as required for great efficacy.
The Dharma Seal of the Great Majestic Secret Flying Sky Alms Bowl (Concluded)
